title: Label content for oral-liquid-single-dose, single-drug-single-dose and multi-drug-single-dose packages and removable cells
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.08(5), a licensee shall label each oral-liquid-single dose, single-drug-single-dose, and multi-drug-single-dose package with: (a) information required by M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 and USP for each medication in the package; (b) the name, strength, physical description, and total quantity of each drug dispensed; (c) the dispensing or preparation date; (d) a beyond-use date, which may not exceed the shortest expiration date on the original manufacturer's container or 60 days, for each drug contained in a multi-drug-single-dose package; and (e) the telephone number of the pharmacy. Under 247 CMR 9.08(6), if the compliance package has removable cells, a pharmacy shall label each cell with a label of sufficient size to properly and clearly label each cell with each drug name and strength.
exam_relevance: Tests the added label elements on compliance packages beyond the statutory prescription label: physical description and total quantity, dispensing or preparation date, the multi-drug-single-dose beyond-use date capped at the shortest manufacturer expiration date or 60 days, the pharmacy telephone number, and cell-by-cell labels for removable cells.

numeric_facts.fact: Longest beyond-use date for each drug in a multi-drug-single-dose package
numeric_facts.conditions: Not to exceed the shortest expiration date on the original manufacturer's container or 60 days

common_confusions: Applying the 60-day beyond-use cap when a manufacturer's container expires sooner; the date may not exceed whichever limit comes first.
Labeling only the outer card of a package whose cells can be removed.
verification_notes: Read in the official mass.gov PDF of 247 CMR 9.00 (every page stamped 12/6/24, with the note Mass. Register #1536, 12/6/2024), decoded in full with no stream decoding failures, during the authoring session of 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-17.
